mechanism.the_test: crates/pa-core/tests/extension_runner.rs::dead_sidecar_degrades_to_errors_not_panics (pa-CORE, not pa-daemon - the backlog note's pa-daemon attribution corrected): spawns the node extension sidecar, asserts is_alive, kills it with platform::kill_pid(pid, Signal::Kill) (libc::kill SIGKILL - returns as soon as the signal is QUEUED, no wait for process teardown), then immediately calls ExtensionRunner::execute_tool('hello') and asserts the error text contains 'sidecar stopped'; then asserts !is_alive(), the registry still bridges 1 tool, and shutdown() succeeds.
mechanism.the_three_racing_arms: RpcClient::request (pa-core/src/extensions/client.rs) detects sidecar death on three paths that race the sidecar's asynchronous do_exit (the kernel tears the process down on another CPU and closes its pipe fds somewhere inside the kill() -> write window): (GREEN/dominant arm) the request line is written to ChildStdin BEFORE do_exit closes the read end - the write lands in the pipe buffer, the stdout read_loop then sees EOF, mark_dead('stdout closed') drains the pending oneshot with RpcError 'extension sidecar stopped: stdout closed', and request returns 'extension RPC call 'tool_execute' failed: extension sidecar stopped: stdout closed' - the asserted substring MATCHES; (RED arm - observed 3/3 in the fleet) do_exit closes the pipe read end BEFORE the write - write_line fails with EPIPE, request returns 'write extension RPC request: Broken pipe (os error 32)' - NO 'sidecar stopped' -> the assert! panics ('death reason missing: extension tool execution failed: ...', extension_runner.rs:248:5 on the 09-25 head / :250:5 on the 09-27 heads); (third arm, unobserved) the read_loop's EOF mark_dead completes before the request's is_alive() check - request returns 'extension sidecar is not running' - also no match.
mechanism.the_designed_contract_holds_in_every_arm: This is a TEST-side assertion race, NOT a product bug: the designed crash-isolation contract (design doc section 2.4) is that a dead sidecar DEGRADES TO ERRORS, NEVER PANICS - and every arm is an error: execute_tool returns Err, no product panic path runs, is_alive() flips false, the registry view keeps the registrations (the bridge_tools call in the test passes in the red runs' own logs - only the death-reason assert fails first), and shutdown handles the already-dead child. The test pins the GREEN arm's exact error text and panics on two other equally-valid error arms.
mechanism.why_load_makes_it_observable: The race window is the microseconds between libc::kill() returning and the request's stdin write: on an idle box the write wins (lands in the buffer -> the green arm); under co-scheduled load the test thread can be descheduled inside that window while do_exit completes on another CPU - the write then hits the closed read end -> EPIPE (the red arm). Exposure is same-binary co-scheduling inside tests/extension_runner.rs (its 7 tokio tests x their own node sidecars run in parallel on the shared vCPUs) amplified by host-level co-scheduling (the fleet pool VMs share the host box with other fleet VMs - the same load regime that fires the compaction pair and worker::turn_stream members, which co-fired in 2 of the 3 reds). Solo invocations are structurally near-immune (the window shrinks to the write-before-teardown arm).
mechanism.provenance: The racing code is stable: pa-core/src/extensions/client.rs request/mark_dead/read_loop unchanged since the port (f492609c6; only the #2771 doc-lint reflow since), the test file unchanged since #2807 (the stage-5 lint reflow that moved the assert from line 248 to 250 between the two red eras); the test is byte-identical at the current tip 07f42eaa3.
